summary.en: A **phrasal verb** is a verb plus a small word (a particle such as _up_, _out_, _off_ or _back_) that together have their own meaning, often different from the verb alone: _give up_ (stop), _turn down_ (refuse), _set off_ (start a journey). Some have no object (_The plane took off._). Others have one, and then you must check whether the verb is **separable** (_switch the light off_ / _switch off the light_) or **inseparable** (_look after the children_). With a pronoun, a separable verb always splits: **switch it off**. They are very common in speech and informal writing; in a formal email you will often choose a one-word verb instead (_postpone_, not _put off_).
summary.es: Un phrasal verb es verbo + partícula (up, out, off…) con significado propio, casi nunca la suma literal de las dos partes. Con pronombre, el objeto va en medio: *turn it off*, nunca *turn off it*. Aprende cada verbo como una palabra más, con su significado y su estructura.

form: No object: **verb + particle** (_wake up_, _break down_, _take off_, _grow up_)
Separable: **verb + object + particle** or **verb + particle + noun** (_call the meeting off_ / _call off the meeting_)
Separable with a pronoun: **verb + pronoun + particle** only (_call it off_)
Inseparable: **verb + particle + object**, always together (_run into an old friend_, _get over a cold_)
Common particles: **up** (finish, increase), **down** (reduce, fail), **out** (disappear, find), **off** (leave, cancel), **on** (continue), **back** (return), **away**
Passive: the object becomes the subject (_The match was called off._)

uses.text: **Everyday actions** → _Please turn the music down; I'm trying to study._
**Changing plans** → _They had to call off the wedding at the last minute._
**Starting and stopping** → _She gave up her job and set up her own company._
**Informal speech** → _Can you pick me up at the station?_

note.en: In Speaking part 4 these verbs make your English sound natural; in a formal email prefer collect, cancel or postpone.
note.es: En Speaking suenan naturales; en un correo formal usa collect, cancel o postpone.

uses.text: **One verb, several meanings** → _take off_ (a plane leaves the ground; clothes come off; a business becomes successful).

mistakes.wrong: Please turn off it before you leave.
mistakes.right: Please turn it off before you leave.

why.en: A pronoun object of a separable phrasal verb goes between the verb and the particle.
why.es: Con pronombre, va en medio: turn it off, pick me up, put them away.

mistakes.wrong: I grew in a small village near Valencia.
mistakes.right: I grew up in a small village near Valencia.

why.en: The meaning of becoming an adult needs the particle; grow alone means to get bigger.
why.es: «Criarse» es grow up; grow solo significa crecer o cultivar.

mistakes.wrong: He gave up to smoke last year.
mistakes.right: He gave up smoking last year.

why.en: Give up is followed by a noun or an -ing form, not to + infinitive.
why.es: Tras give up va -ing: give up smoking.

mistakes.wrong: Can you pick up me at the airport?
mistakes.right: Can you pick me up at the airport?

why.en: Pronouns (me, him, it, them) never come after the particle of a separable verb.
why.es: El pronombre nunca va detrás de la partícula.

examples.en: My car broke down on the motorway, so I called a garage.
examples.es: Se me estropeó el coche en la autopista, así que llamé a un taller.

examples.en: Our flight took off an hour late because of the fog.
I found a wallet in the street and handed it in at the police station.
examples.es: Encontré una cartera en la calle y la entregué en la comisaría.

examples.en: Could you put those boxes away before the guests arrive?
She turned down the job because the salary was too low.
I ran into my old teacher at the supermarket yesterday.
We set off at six to avoid the traffic.
He's still getting over the flu, so he isn't working this week.
The organisers called off the concert because of the storm.
If you don't know a word, look it up in a dictionary.
Hold on a moment, I'll check my diary.
examples.es: Espera un momento, miro mi agenda.

practice.prompt: Those boxes are in the way. Please ___.

explanation.en: A pronoun object of a separable phrasal verb goes between the verb and the particle.

practice.prompt: I found a wallet outside the cinema, so I ___ at the police station.

explanation.en: Hand in is separable, so the pronoun it goes in the middle: handed it in.

practice.prompt: My old teacher was shopping at the same supermarket yesterday, and I ___ by the fruit stall.

explanation.en: Run into (meet by chance) is inseparable: the object always follows the particle.

practice.prompt: My car ___ on the motorway, so we were late for the wedding.

explanation.en: Break down has no object here, so nothing follows the particle.
